neighbours.label: verb of consulting a source to get information ('look' up, 'read', 'find', 'check') in instructions, where the object is a reference, label or record
fire: If you forget the password, you can look up the reset code in the welcome email we sent.
Before you buy the cereal, take a moment to read the ingredients printed on the side of the box.
To renew online, simply find your member number on the back of your library card.
I always have to look up the exact flags for the tar command whenever I use it.
The footnote lets you read the original Latin passage that the author is quoting.
Students should check the timetable posted outside room 12 for their exam slot.
When the error appears, look in the log file for the line that mentions the failed module.
Patients can find their appointment time in the reminder letter from the clinic.
quiet: If you forget the password, you can request a new account from the help desk instead.
Before you buy the cereal, take a moment to compare the prices of the store brands.
To renew online, simply pay the annual fee with any major credit card.
I always have to type the tar command twice because I make small mistakes.
The footnote explains why the author left the Latin passage untranslated.
Students should arrive early outside room 12 on the day of their exam.
When the error appears, restart the service and wait for the module to reload.
Patients can bring a relative with them to the appointment at the clinic.

notes: Card: ' look' x5, ' read' x3, ' find', ' Look'; contexts are 'I need to look up the syntax', 'allows you to read the original reference', 'find your account number on your mailing label'. Logit effect suppresses records/calendars/databases/maps, the places one consults. Near misses use non-consulting verbs in the same instructional frame.
